title: deployment-arbitrage-optimizer-notes
body:
Purpose:
Quick working sheet & recommendations for an "arbitrage" style decision tool that surface when private deployment (on‑prem or VPC) beats hosted economics given customer constraints (latency, compliance, sustained throughput). Focus: combine hardware amortization, license/support bundles, ops headcount, network/storage, and elasticity overhead into a compact scenario matrix.

High level approach / requirements:
- Produce a small set (4) of canonical scenarios for sales & solutions engineering to present: "CapEx single-tenant", "Cloud Reserved VPC", "Hybrid burst (reserved + burst to hosted)", "Colo finance-lease".
- Output: break-even months, incremental monthly savings vs hosted list price, sensitivity bands for utilization (+-20%), and recommended license/support packaging to maximize margin for Redwood while staying competitive.
- Keep model granular enough to highlight levers: GPU count, utilization, model memory (affects choice of instance type), license-per-GPU vs per-node pricing, support tier % of license, amortization window (3/4/5 years), and tax/financing cost.

Assumptions table (baseline example inputs):
- Target throughput: 30M tokens/day (sustained) ~ 900M tokens/month
- Effective tokens per GPU-hour (inference mix): 2.5M tokens/hour (baseline medium prompt mix)
- GPUs required (rounded): GPUs_needed = ceil((monthly_tokens / (hours_per_month * tokens_per_gpu_hour)))
  - hours_per_month = 24 * 30 = 720
  - GPUs_needed baseline = ceil(900M / (720 * 2.5M)) = ceil(900 / 1800) => GPUs_needed = 1 (this shows sensitivity to tokens_per_gpu_hour — realistic workloads will need tens/hundreds; treat for demo only)
- Baseline pricing (examples):
  - On-prem GPU unit cost (CapEx per GPU): $12,000 (A100 class equivalent)
  - Colocation per GPU/month (rack, power, network): $800
  - Cloud reserved instance equivalent per GPU/month: $3,200 (1yr reserved)
  - Hosted API blended cost (Redwood hosted list price) per GPU-equivalent-token-run: $X (we map to per-token later)
  - License (one-time/per-GPU amortized): $6,000 per GPU (can be converted to per-month)
  - Support bundles: Standard = 12% of license annually, Premium = 25%
  - Ops FTE cost (infra + SRE + on-call apportioned): $220,000/year per 1 FTE -> apportioned per number of GPUs assumed: 1 FTE per 40 GPUs (baseline)
  - Network egress (customer-facing): $0.09/GB (applies more to VPC/cloud)
  - Storage & snapshotting: $0.02/GB/month (persistent model store)
  - Financing (effective cost of capital for CapEx amort): 6% annual
  - Depreciation/amortization window: 36 months default

Canonical scenarios (worked example, simplified):
Columns: scenario | GPUs procured | CapEx | Monthly amortization | Monthly colo/cloud cost | Monthly license/support | Monthly ops allocation | Network & storage | Total monthly cost | Breakeven vs hosted
1) CapEx single-tenant (on-prem) | 16 GPUs | CapEx = 16 * $12k = $192k | Monthly amort = (192k + 16*6k license)/36 = (192k + 96k)/36 = 288k/36 = $8,000 | Colo cost = 16 * $0 (assuming in-house DC) -> $0 or internal power charge $400/mo -> $6,400 | License/support monthly = (96k amort)/36 + support (12%*96k)/12 = 2,666 + 960 = ~3,626 | Ops allocation = (16/40)*220k/12 = 0.4*18,333 = $7,333 | Net & storage = 16*(avg egress/storage) => $320 | Total monthly = 8,000 + 6,400 + 3,626 + 7,333 + 320 = $25,679 | Compare to hosted baseline (e.g. hosted cost = $35k/month) => monthly savings ~ $9,321 -> break-even immediate vs CapEx payback since amort included; compute months to recoup initial extra implementation/onboarding (~$40k) -> ~4.3 months

2) VPC Reserved | 16 GPU-equivalents (reserved) | CapEx 0 | Monthly reserved compute = 16 * $3,200 = $51,200 | License/support: license per-GPU still applies for Private deploy, but vendor may reprice: assume license = $3k/GPU amortized => monthly = 16*3k/36 = $1,333 + support premium (15%) = $400 | Ops allocation = cloud-managed lower ops -> 0.2 FTE per 40 GPUs -> (16/40)*110k/12 = $3,667 | Network & storage = $1,600 | Total monthly = 51,200 + 1,733 + 3,667 + 1,600 = $58,200 | Hosted baseline (35k) -> worse for this scale; break-even only when utilization > 80% AND cloud reserved discount deeper or when egress drives hosted pricing even higher

3) Hybrid (reserve 8 GPUs + burst to Redwood hosted) | Reserve monthly compute = 8 * 3,200 = 25,600 | Hosted burst variable cost = leftover demand * hosted per-token pricing (sensitive) -> example $12k | License/support apportioned = 8*3k/36 + support = $667 + $200 = $867 | Ops ~ $2k | Total monthly = 25,600 + 12,000 + 867 + 2,000 + net = $40,467 -> compare to fully hosted 35k -> hybrid slightly higher but reduces CapEx and increases flexibility

4) Colocation + lease finance | 16 GPUs | CapEx financed with 4yr lease at 5% => monthly lease payment ~ $4,400 (for GPU principal+interest) | Colo recurring = 16 * $800 = 12,800 | License/support monthly = $3,626 (same as on-prem) | Ops = $7,333 | Total monthly = 4,400 + 12,800 + 3,626 + 7,333 + net = $28,159 -> closer to hosted but with more predictable latency/compliance guarantees

Key sensitivity levers / what to surface in calculator UI:
- Utilization delta: small changes in sustained utilization (±20%) swing GPU count and amortization per-unit dramatically. Show charts for break-even utilization thresholds.
- License model: per-GPU vs per-deployment vs per-query. Per-GPU benefits scale-heavy customers; per-query helps short-term, high-variance customers. Provide a toggle.
- Support tier selection: show 12% vs 25% tiers and what value add justifies premium (SLA, War-room response, code-level fixes).
- Model quantization & batchability: if quantization reduces GPU memory footprint it changes instance class and effective tokens/hour (improves economics). Allow multiplier input.
- Upgrade cadence: 3yr vs 4yr amortization move monthly amortization by ~25% — vital for colo vs lease decisions.
- Network egress: present region-specific egress rates; for burst-to-hosted scenarios egress can kill the hybrid case.

Operational recommendations for sales/solutions engineering (short checklist):
1) Capture expected sustained QPS/tokens and daily distribution (peaky vs flat). If >60% sustained util, favor private reserved; if <30% favor hosted.
2) Validate compliance & data residency — if SOC2/P2P encryption and KMS isolation required, there are cost adders (KMS/HSM, audit retention) that we surface as "compliance uplift" percent.
3) Offer license packaging: "starter" (pay-per-node amortization), "scale" (per-GPU discount at >32 GPUs), and "enterprise flat" (annual commit for a fixed fee covering bursts). Provide recommended margin targets per band.
4) Recommend a Hybrid kickoff: start with reserved for baseline 30-60% capacity and outsource bursts to Redwood hosted for peaks, re-evaluate every quarter.
5) For colo customers run a sensitivity: if colo power & rack > $1k/GPU/month, fallback to VPC or Lease.

Next steps & product asks:
- Build a minimal web calculator (internal) using this model: inputs: monthly tokens, token distribution (peak factor), desired latency SLA, compliance flags, license preference, amortization years. Outputs: scenario table + recommended bundle and "talking points" for AE.
- Add toggles for quantization uplift and batching multipliers.
- Instrument real customer pilots: capture actual tokens/GPU-hour metrics and replace our 2.5M baseline with measured values; refine GPU-equivalent pricing mapping.
- Create a short AE playbook with 3 sample customer vignettes (SaaS PLG scale, regulated enterprise, and AI-native high-throughput) and pre-calculated recommended packages.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm typical tokens/GPU-hour for our supported model catalog (ask applied-ml to produce a small table by model family).
- Agree on license floor/discount tiers with finance and legal (per-GPU vs per-instance).
- Validate ops FTE allocation assumptions with SRE/solutions-eng (we might be underestimating 24/7 coverage cost).

Notes to self (scratch):
- If customer has existing GPUs on balance sheet, treat transfer price + support as important negotiation lever (we can offer cheap support-only on older HW).
- Consider an "UPSIDE" metric: how much additional revenue Redwood can extract via higher support SLA and managed services beyond baseline license.

Appendix: quick formulas (copy/paste into sheet)
- monthly_amort = (capex + license_total) / amort_months + capex * financing_rate / 12
- gpus_needed = ceil(monthly_tokens / (hours_per_month * tokens_per_gpu_hour))
- ops_monthly = (gpus / 40) * FTE_cost_ann / 12
- total_monthly = monthly_amort + recurring_compute + license_support_monthly + ops_monthly + network_storage
- break_even_months = onboarding_cost / monthly_savings_vs_hosted

End of sheet — this is a working draft for discussion, not final pricing.
